key_insight: Natural-image pretraining improved medical diffusion image generation, with benefits linked to spatial structure rather than semantic understanding.
clinical_relevance: Better synthetic-image fidelity may support medical imaging research, but the reported proxy measures do not establish clinical utility or safety.
method: Compared natural-image initialization with training from scratch across pixel- and latent-space diffusion models.
Evaluated models with 131M–952M parameters on RadImageNet and BraTS.
Probed denoiser representations and tested mixed-domain training, medical pretraining, and reinitialization.
evidence_signal: Natural-image initialization improved relative gFID by 21–34% in pixel space and 14% in latent space; gains aligned with pathology-classification and radiomic-feature fidelity proxies.
watch_item: Findings are limited to the studied datasets and setups; clinical fidelity was assessed through proxies rather than demonstrated patient-care outcomes.
paper_title: From Natural Images to Medical Scans: Transferability of Diffusion Models for Medical Image Generation
